question: to the Commission Nadine Morano (PPE) Subject:

The war in Iran and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz have led to a sharp rise in gas prices, which have reached EUR 54 per MWh – an increase of almost 80 % since the start of the conflict. This energy inflation threatens not only the EU industries that rely on gas, but also the purchasing power of households. It also risks re-igniting inflation in Europe, which was only just starting to be brought under control thanks to the efforts of the European Central Bank. With this in mind and given that, at the tail end of winter, European gas reserves are less than 25 % full, could the Commission answer the following question: How does it plan to rebuild these stocks in preparation for winter 2026‑2027 and to guarantee access to affordable gas for businesses and households?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.6.2026) The EU’s strategy to rebuild gas stocks ahead of winter 2026-2027 focuses on adapting to the current price volatility stemming from the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz, which has narrowed the summer-winter price spread discouraging gas injections. To counter this, the Commission has taken proactive steps to ensure that the EU achieves an adequate storage level ahead of next winter while mitigating price volatility. On 20 March 2026, the Commissioner for Energy and Housing invited Member States to make full use of the flexibilities from the Storage Regulation1 and lower the storage target by up to 10 percentage points from 90% to 80%, reducing overall EU storage needs by 10 billion cubic meters while still being sufficient for next winter. The European Network of Transmission System Operators for Gas (ENTSOG)’s summer supply outlook confirmed that EU infrastructure is sufficiently flexible to allow 80% of storage filling by November 2026 in the event of limited liquified natural gas supply. To achieve this level of storage filling, an early start of injections would allow a longer injection period, limiting pressure on prices and avoiding an end-of-summer rush as happened in 2022. The Commission presented on 22 April 2026 the AccelerateEU Communication2 with immediate targeted actions aimed at better protecting households and industry from high energy prices. As announced the Commission is facilitating the coordination of national action on gas storage filling in the regular meetings of the Gas Coordination Group. The Commission also stands ready to assess a further increase of the permitted deviation threshold (up to an additional 5%) under the updated EU Gas Storage Regulation.
